newsitem.title: USA: NEW PRODUCTS - Print Club sticker-mania arriving in U.S.
newsitem.headline: NEW PRODUCTS - Print Club sticker-mania arriving in U.S.

text.p: The latest rage sweeping Japan is coming soon to a video arcade near you -- sticker mania.

"Print Club" is a personalized photo sticker machine that puts the user into the picture with a choice of celebrities and animated characters. The sheets of 16 personalized stickers are collected, traded, used for labeling personal items -- just about anything.
Since its introduction in Japan in 1995, Print Club has gotten so popular that users have coined a word, "Pricla" (pronounced pree-kla), to describe the activity.

About 70 percent of "Pricla" users are female, and it is a hit with young teenage girls. But it's also becoming increasingly popular among boys, men and women, and more than 1.5 million Japanese "Pricla" every day.
Developed by Tokyo-based Atlus Co. Ltd., Print Club will be introduced into the United States at the June 10-12 Licensing '97 International Show at New York's Jacob Javitz Convention Centre.

Here's how it works: Users go to video arcades, grocery stores, shopping centres or fast-food restaurants -- wherever there is a Print Club. The free-standing machine has a 20-inch monitor and a user stands in front of the screen.
After selecting what type of "frame" is wanted -- ranging from cartoon characters, television personalities, pop music stars, film stars or sports figures -- the user has his or her picture taken.

It costs $3 to use Print Club, and the result is a page of 16 stickers that can be used, traded or saved. In Japan there are accessories that go with Print Club stickers, such as key chains, pins, toys and protective covers.
Just when cyber-pets were catching on ...
Fiskars Inc., the Wausau, Wisc.-based maker of school supplies for children and adults, has introduced washable tempera paint markers for children ages 4 and up.
Special applicators allow smooth flow of paint and eliminate spills. The soft tip can be left uncovered for 72 hours without drying out, the company said.
The tempera paint is non-toxic, washable and comes in a variety of colours.
Sets contain three two-ounce bottles of paint. The plastic bottles are large enough to be easily grasped by small children.
Individual paints cast $2.80 each. Sets of three colours sell for about $7 and sets of $12 sell for about $12.50.
For more information, call the company at 1-800-950-0203.
The newest product to enter the tooth whitening market is Mentadent's Advanced Whitening Toothpaste, which is hitting store shelves now.
The toothpaste contains fluoride, baking soda, peroxide and zinc citrate, which as been proveen to be effective in inhibiting the formation of tartar, Mentadent said.

Chesebrough-Pond's USA said that one-third of 116 people in a test who brushed with Mentadent Advanced Whitening toothpaste began to see a difference in the whiteness of their teeth after two weeks. After two months of twice a day use, 60 percent of the panellists saw between a one- and three-shade increase in whiteness.
Mentadent Advanced Whitening comes in a dual-chamber pump, like original Mentadent.
The average retail price for the 3.5-ounce pump and 5.2-ounce refill is $3.29, and the 5.2-ounce pump sells for $3.69.
Lancome, the French cosmetics and fragrances company, is adding to its line of the fragrance Poeme, with a scented body powder that should be available in September.
Lancome also said it is packaging Poeme, its 30th fragrance in 60 years, in a special-edition bottle, with a portion of the proceeds donated to Reading Is Fundamental Inc.
Reading is Fundamental is a nationwide volunteer literacy organisation.
The-special edition bottle is currently only available at Saks Fifth Avenue's flagship store, but a spokeswoman said it could be available elsewhere in the future.
Poeme perfume sells for $55 for a 1.7-ounce bottle.
